The high-profile Legends Football Game will bring together some of the continent’s most celebrated former internationals in a special encounter celebrating three decades since Nigeria conquered Africa and claimed Olympic football gold.
Leading the African contingent are former African Footballer of the Year Adebayor, Senegalese forward Diouf, Ivorian midfielder Zokora and former Ghana captain Appiah, whose contributions to African football earned them recognition on the global stage.
Other notable names expected to feature include Ghanaian duo John Paintsil and Anthony Baffoe, Senegal’s Khalilou Fadiga, Burkina Faso’s Aristide Bancé, Cameroon’s Rigobert Song and Alexandre Song, Zimbabwe’s Peter Ndlovu and Benjani Mwaruwari, as well as South African goalkeeper Brian Baloyi.
They will face a formidable Super Eagles Legends side drawn from Nigeria’s celebrated 1994 and 1996 generations, in what promises to be a nostalgic reunion of players who shaped one of the country’s most successful periods in international football.
Nigeria won the 1994 Africa Cup of Nations in Tunisia before securing the men’s football gold medal at the 1996 Atlanta Olympic Games, becoming the first African nation to achieve the feat.
The event is being organised by Toptier Sports Management in partnership with Afreximbank and CANEX, with the aim of celebrating the achievements and enduring influence of African football icons.
Chichi Nwoko, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Toptier Sports Management, said the game would provide an opportunity to recognise former players whose exploits helped raise the profile of African football.
“These are names that every football fan in Africa knows. We are proud to bring them to Lagos to honour the heroes of 1994 and 1996,” she said.
The encounter is expected to attract football fans keen to relive the memorable moments of African football’s golden era, with the gates opening at 1.30pm.
For supporters unable to attend the match at the stadium, the game will be broadcast live on NTA, AIT and Silverbird between 5pm and 7pm.
With several household names from across the continent expected in Lagos, the Legends Football Game promises an evening of nostalgia, rivalry and celebration of the players who helped put African football on the global map.
